Raw storage of a zuint vector

Source: R/types.R
zu_storage.Rd

zu_storage() returns the payload a zuint vector is stored in, for code that reads the bits directly: a double vector whose bits are 64-bit integers for int64 and uint64, and a complex vector whose real and imaginary parts hold the low and high 64-bit words for int128 and uint128. zu_from_storage() reverses it. Names are kept both ways.

Usage

zu_storage(x)

zu_from_storage(payload, type)

Arguments

x

A zuint vector.

payload

A double or complex vector, as returned by zu_storage().

type

One of "int64", "uint64", "int128" or "uint128".

Value

zu_storage() returns a double or complex vector; zu_from_storage() a zuint vector of type.

Details

The payload is not a number: printing it or computing with it is meaningless. Keeping the representation behind these two functions is what lets it change without breaking callers.

Examples

p <- zu_storage(int128(-1))
p
#> [1] NaN+NaNi
zu_from_storage(p, "int128")
#> <int128[1]>
#> [1] -1
